decisions.reason: After surviving a second year, this core-adjacent upholstery fabric likely meets at least satisfactory aspiration levels, so a medium-sized firm with some slack would usually retain it.
Its weaker prominence still suggests more uncertain demand, but continued market presence implies results have not fallen far enough below aspiration to justify withdrawal yet.
Its strong fit with the curtain range and contract-relevant flame-retardant functionality make it likely to perform above aspiration and remain in the portfolio.
This product draws on existing design and material capabilities, and although probably not a star, it is close enough to the core business for management to keep while monitoring performance.

E remains the most niche and potentially weakest fit with aspiration levels, but organizational slack and its relatedness to the established collection still make retention slightly more likely than discontinuation.
As a newer but prominently presented fabric spanning upholstery and curtains, F is still in its evaluation phase and would typically be kept unless early results clearly disappoint.
